info.title: Wardrik
info.description: Wardrik's operations. Each is named by its operationId, everywhere it's offered: over HTTP, in the CLI, as an agent's tool. x-wardrik-action is what a caller must be allowed to do, x-wardrik-effect whether it reads, changes or destroys, and x-wardrik-subject what it acts on: one agent, many agents, or the deployment. An agent the caller reaches none of is answered as one that doesn't exist. A route on one of an agent's conversations names its operation in x-wardrik-operation, and has no operationId of its own. A hook or a channel takes a request as a service sent it, over HTTP; x-wardrik-input is what the operation takes from it, and x-wardrik-output what it answers.

200.description: The agents.

delete.description: Removes each agent in the same way as agent.forget. The agent is stopped, and its conversations, definition and triggers are deleted.

Each call, with its agent.

get.description: A page returns the events after the cursor, or from the start without one. A stream returns the events after the cursor, or only new events without one. If older events were deleted past the cursor, a wardrik.events.dropped event comes first and reading continues from the oldest event kept.

200.description: A page of their logs after the cursor, or with Accept: text/event-stream their logs as server-sent events, after the cursor and then as they are written. Each event's id is the cursor after it.

get.summary: Read the latest event cursor for agents

200.description: The cursor at the end of each log the agents cover.
Its snapshot.

put.description: Creates the agent from this definition, or updates a running agent from its next turn. Each call replaces the whole definition. An unsupported key returns not_supported with the key's name.

200.description: The agent, started, or brought to the definition from its next turn.

204.description: Forgotten: stopped, with its conversation, definition and triggers deleted.

put.summary: Create or update an agent's trigger
put.description: Creates or updates one trigger and saves it in the agent's definition. Returns not_found if the agent has no definition. If every and timezone don't change, the next run time is kept.

200.description: The trigger, with its name.
The trigger, as it was.

post.summary: Deliver a webhook request to a trigger
post.description: Runs the agent once for a request sent to its webhook trigger, after checking the request against the trigger's secret. A request that fails the check returns not_found, the same as a missing trigger. unavailable means the agent can't run now and the service should retry later.

requestBody.description: The request a service sent, as it came, in any content type. Its headers go along too, since a signature covers the exact body.

202.description: Taken: the agent is asked about it, once.

post.summary: Deliver a webhook request with the secret in the path
post.description: Works like hook.deliver, for services that only accept a URL. The secret is the last path segment of the URL. Keep this URL as private as an API token.

requestBody.description: The request a service sent, as it came, in any content type. Its headers go along too, since a signature covers the exact body.

202.description: Taken: the agent is asked about it, once.

post.summary: Reload agent definitions
post.description: Running agents use their current definition from their next turn. Sleeping agents use it when they wake. If you set agents, only those agents are updated. The node that handles the request also reloads its agent declarations, MCP servers and triggers.

200.description: The nodes that read them.
The nodes, with how many agents run on each, and how many sleep.

get.description: Returns memory, CPU and process figures for each node, and the running agents that use the most memory. Measuring scheduler use takes 250 ms.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of agents to return. Defaults to 20.

200.description: Resource use for each node, and the agents that use the most memory.

post.summary: Move an agent to another node
post.description: Restarts the agent on the given node, with its state. A turn in progress is stopped, and pending approvals are dropped. Send the request again after the move.

200.description: The agent, on the node it moved to.

post.summary: Deliver a chat app request to a channel
post.description: Passes a request from a chat app such as Slack, unchanged, to the channel with this name. The channel verifies it, for example by its signature, and responds in the format the chat app expects. Returns not_found if no channel with this name accepts requests.

requestBody.description: The request a chat app sent, as it came, in any content type. Its headers go along too, since a signature covers the exact body.

200.description: The channel's answer, as the chat app expects it: the channel's status, headers and body.

agent.name: agent
agent.description: The agent ID, URL-encoded as one path segment.

interrupt.name: interrupt
interrupt.description: The ID of the pending tool call.

agents.name: agents
agents.description: Agent IDs, each listed once. Each includes its conversations. Defaults to every agent you can access.

named_agents.name: agents
named_agents.description: Agent IDs to read, each listed once. Each includes its conversations.

types.name: types
types.description: The event types to return, for example wardrik.run.completed. List each type once. Defaults to all types. wardrik.events.dropped is always returned.

after.name: after
after.description: Return events after this cursor. Use the next value from the previous page, an event ID from a stream, or the cursor from agent.read, agent.timeline or agent.runs.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: The maximum number to return. Defaults to 100.

starting_after.name: starting_after
starting_after.description: Return events after this sequence number. Use the next value from the previous page.

secret.name: secret
secret.description: The webhook secret, for services that accept only a URL.

channel.name: channel
channel.description: The channel name, as configured on the server.

path.name: path
path.description: The endpoint within the channel that receives the request, such as events.

conversation.name: conversation
conversation.description: The conversation ID, URL-encoded as one path segment. A conversation uses the agent's definition and has its own history.

Unauthorized.description: No credential, or one that isn't known or has expired: unauthorized.

Forbidden.description: The caller may not do this: forbidden.

NotFound.description: No such agent, or one the caller doesn't reach: not_found.

Conflict.description: It conflicts with what's there, like a call the agent doesn't wait on: conflict.

NotSupported.description: What was asked isn't supported here yet.

Unavailable.description: It can't be done now; try again later.
